title: Year 12 Investigating Science Module 5 – Scientific Investigations
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 12 Investigating Science Module 5, organised by its four Inquiry Questions. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What often begins a scientific investigation by revealing something worth explaining?
What testable statement gives a possible explanation for an observation?
Which scientists investigated the bacterial cause of peptic ulcers?
questions.answer: Marshall and Warren. Accept: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren.

questions.prompt: Which scientist investigated plant growth using a willow tree experiment?
questions.answer: Jan Baptista van Helmont. Accept: van Helmont.

questions.prompt: Which engineer’s observation of a melted chocolate bar contributed to the development of microwave cooking?
What may unexpected results cause scientists to do to an original hypothesis?

categories.name: What methodology best suits an investigation?

questions.prompt: What investigation type involves deliberately changing a variable under controlled conditions?
What investigation type collects observations directly in a natural environment?
What investigation type gathers responses from a selected group of people?
What investigation type uses a simplified representation of a real system?
questions.answer: Modelling. Accept: a model or simulation.

questions.prompt: Which scientist estimated Earth’s circumference using shadows and geometry?
What type of published literature should be checked when judging whether an investigation is relevant to existing science?
What term describes whether an investigation measures what it was intended to measure?
What term describes the consistency of results when measurements or investigations are repeated?
What variable is deliberately changed by the investigator?
What variable is measured as the outcome?
What variables are kept constant to help make a fair test?
Increasing a representative sample size generally improves what aspect of confidence in the results?

categories.name: What is the structure of an investigative report?

questions.prompt: Which report section states what the investigation was designed to find out?
Which report section explains how the investigation was carried out?
Which report section presents the collected observations and measurements?
Which report section interprets results and explains their meaning?
Which report section states whether the findings support the hypothesis?
What formal process evaluates scientific work before publication in many journals?

finalRound.prompt: What two qualities are checked by asking whether an investigation measures what it should and whether its results are consistent?
